subject: Urgent: Atlas ML — latency spikes due to KV cache pinning (executive escalation)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops@atlasml.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-30T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Severe latency/error spikes — suspect KV cache pinning

Priya,

We started seeing a sharp latency increase and elevated 5xx rates on our production workload around 08:50 PST. Throughput dropped ~40% while p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.4s and error rate climbed to 3.2%.

Initial observations from our side:
- Spikes correlate with a traffic burst from a nightly batch that pins a small set of keys (prefix /user/lookup).
- The serving pool serving Atlas has high KV eviction churn; TTLs look normal but hit rate oscillates.
- When the burst ends, latency recovers but then degrades again after a few minutes (oscillation).

Can you confirm if this is a cache "pinning"/hot-key/eviction feedback loop? This is affecting user-facing latency. We are ready to join a bridge.

Attaching a short profile and sample traces.

- Samir
Ops Lead, Atlas ML
[Attachment: kv-cache-profile-20270130.csv (CSV)]

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <ops@atlasml.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-30T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency/error spikes — suspect KV cache pinning

Samir — thanks for the quick note and the profile. We're on it.

Short plan:
1) I will open an incident bridge now and loop Engineering.
2) We'll push a short-term mitigation (temporarily reduce batch size for your route and enable bypass for the pinned prefix) to break the eviction oscillation.
3) Engineering will analyze configuration and propose a durable policy change (per-prefix quotas or segmented LRU).

Can you confirm whether you can tolerate a short config window (~15 minutes) for us to roll the bypass? Also sharing your current traffic ramp schedule would help.

I'll update you in the bridge.

— Priya Natarajan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: atlas-action-plan.pdf (PDF)]

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-30T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: quick analysis — eviction oscillation from pinned keys

Priya / team,

I dug into the profile Samir sent and the pool metrics. Short summary:
- Root cause: high-frequency small-key burst is saturating the KV cache's hot-set eviction logic. The current global LRU combined with a single eviction queue causes repeated evictions and re-inserts for the same prefix. That creates head-of-line blocking on the hot lane and a feedback loop — when the cache misses spike, throughput collapses and latency spikes.
- Repro: I ran the replay against a staging pool and see the same oscillation when the prefix gets pinned.

Proposed mitigations (short -> mid -> long):
SHORT (10–30m, low risk):
- Apply per-prefix bypass config: route /user/lookup to bypass KV for 2 min during bursts.
- Reduce batch size for Atlas route from 64->24 to reduce HOL blocking.

MID (1–3h, moderate risk):
- Increase KV cache partition size for the Atlas serving pool (allocate +15% memory) and enable short-term sticky slots to reduce churn.
- Add circuit-breaker for eviction rate: if eviction/sec > X then temporarily force bypass for offending prefixes.

LONG (days):
- Implement segmented LRU with per-prefix quotas or frequency-tiered caching. Also add prefetch heuristics for recurring prefixes.

I attached a config diff for the short changes (kv-config-diff.patch). We'll need permission to bump pool memory for the mid fix (risk: transient GC/heap pressure in that pool).

Markus
Engineering Lead — Runtime Performance
[Attachment: kv-config-diff.patch (plaintext)]

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <ops@atlasml.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency/error spikes — suspect KV cache pinning

Samir,

Thanks — we rolled the SHORT mitigations at 11:00 PST: batch size reduced and a bypass rule for /user/lookup during bursts. Early telemetry shows p99 reduced to ~320ms and error rate back under 0.4%. Throughput is recovering.

Next steps:
- We'll keep the bypass in place for the next 4 hours while Markus works on the MID changes.
- If you can, please hold off on the nightly batch ramp for one cycle so we can validate behavior.

I'll follow up with an internal exec ask for a temporary capacity bump to make the MID change lower risk. Appreciate the quick signal.

— Priya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-01-30T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Internal: quick analysis — eviction oscillation from pinned keys (exec attention requested)

Priya,

We've validated the MID plan in staging. Expected impact: removing oscillation and restoring stable p99, but it requires a temporary +15% allocation to the Atlas serving pool for ~6 hours and one config rollout window. Estimated cost for the bump (on our reserved pool) is low but measurable; operational risk is minor but non-zero (requeue / GC spikes on the target hosts).

Ask for execs:
- Approval to increase pool allocation immediately (temp) to reduce eviction churn.
- Authorization to offer Atlas a one-time service credit if we use burst-resources beyond their contracted capacity.

If we don't get approval in the next 2 hours we'll continue with SHORT mitigations but the MID fix will be delayed, meaning potential repeated oscillations during heavy bursts.

Rishi
Head of Platform Reliability

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Subject: Executive summary and ask — Atlas ML incident (KV eviction oscillation)

Jonas / Laura — quick executive summary and asks: 

Impact: ongoing customer-facing latency and elevated error rate for Atlas ML during periodic batch bursts. Short mitigations restored service but risk remains until MID changes are applied.

Root cause: eviction oscillation caused by a hot prefix that pins keys, leading to hot-lane head-of-line blocking and repeated cache churn.

Proposed immediate actions (we're ready to execute):
1) Temporary +15% pool allocation to the Atlas serving pool for 6 hours. (Purpose: reduce eviction churn while MID changes deploy.)
2) Authorization to grant a one-time service credit if we need to apply burst capacity beyond contract terms.
3) Greenlight for MID rollout: apply sticky slots + eviction-rate circuit-breaker and monitor for 2 hours before reverting any config.

Implication: cost < $X/day for temporary bump (finance informed), small operational risk during rollout. Failure to approve may lead to repeated customer impact during nightly bursts.

Request: decision within 2 hours so we can proceed before Atlas' next ramp window.

Attached: short technical brief and config diff. Incident ticket: INF-4729.

— Priya Natarajan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
